newsitem.title: HONG KONG: LG Eng to build Caltex LPG terminal in China.
newsitem.headline: LG Eng to build Caltex LPG terminal in China.

text.p: Caltex Ocean Gas and Energy Ltd said on Wednesday it appointed LG Engineering Co Ltd as the major contractor to design and build its 200,000 cubic metre liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) terminal at Shantou, China.

Caltex Ocean Gas and Energy is a joint venture between Caltex China Ltd and Shantou Ocean Enterprise. Caltex is a joint venture between major oil companies Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp. LG Engineering, a member of South Korean conglomerate LG Group, signed an engineering, procurement and construction contract in Shantou on Wednesday, Caltex said in a statement.

Caltex said the Shantou LPG terminal, located at the Guang Ao deep water port in the southern province of Guangdong, will be China's first underground storage caverns and the largest LPG storage base on the mainland.

The Shantou terminal will include one berth of 50,000 tonnage, two berths of 5,000 tonnage, two underground caverns with a capacity of 100,000 cubic metres each for the storage of propane and butane, as well as supporting facilities, it said.
The initial import target is one million tons per year once the plant is completed in 1999, it said.
Financing is expected to be arranged through the International Financing Corp, the private sector arm of the World Bank, and a group of international commercial banks, Caltex said.

China's Market Daily newspaper reported on January 17 that the facility would have a total investment of US$99 million, made up of US$66 million in loans and US$33 million jointly invested by Caltex and Shantou Ocean.
The project has the approval of the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, the newspaper said.
